name: nemotron-3.5-asr-ptbr
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from nvidia/nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b (config.json max_position_embeddings 5000). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: Inherited unchanged from nvidia/nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b: 0 full GQA layers (kv heads 1, head_dim None) and 0 other layers, per the base config.json.
notes: ADDED 2026-11-02. A finetune of nvidia/nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b, not a new base model: same config.json, same 0.6 parameters (identical tensor set). Recorded as a contender because it publishes benchmark evidence against its own base; the evidence rows below are card-sourced and marked vendor_claim. Licence openmdw-1.1, repo created 2026-07-28. CAVEAT: WER/CER are lower-is-better, so the 'higher' win is a lower error rate; the FLEURS row improves only under the card's normalization (raw WER 28.63 vs base 21.93 is worse), and the card itself notes NVIDIA's own FLEURS figure (5.48%) uses different normalization/decoding and is not comparable. CORAA test split was held out from fine-tuning.

benchmarks.name: CORAA test WER (normalized)
benchmarks.config: Card table '| Modelo | WER raw | WER norm | CER norm |' on the official CORAA test split (12,676 samples, ~17.6h): base NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 ASR zero-shot 31.87 vs this model 20.96 (raw 45.64 vs 20.97). Identical text normalization applied to reference and hypothesis; greedy RNNT, offline batch, NeMo 2.8.0rc0. Test split excluded from fine-tuning (train used CORAA train/val + MLS PT + CV9).

benchmarks.name: CORAA test CER (normalized)
benchmarks.config: Same table, base 20.64 vs this model 10.89.

benchmarks.name: FLEURS pt-BR test WER (normalized)
benchmarks.config: Card table on google/fleurs config pt_br, test split (919 samples): base zero-shot 13.86 vs this model 10.37 (raw 21.93 vs 28.63). CAVEAT: raw WER is worse than base on FLEURS; the card notes the NVIDIA base card itself reports 5.48% FLEURS Portuguese under a different normalization/decoding, so this row is a same-table comparison only in the card's own normalization.
